steps.title: The Saar
steps.body: The Saar joins the Mosel near Trier. It's cooler and windier than the Middle Mosel, and for centuries grapes ripened fully only in good years. In warm years, its Rieslings are among the most precise and electric in the world, with steely acidity. Scharzhofberg, owned largely by Egon Müller, is its most famous vineyard.

steps.title: The Ruwer
steps.body: The Ruwer is a small tributary near Trier, with only a few estates. Its wines are delicate, floral and racy. Maximin Grünhaus and Karthäuserhofberg are famous estates, both former monastic properties. Like the Saar, it was officially part of the Mosel-Saar-Ruwer region until 2007, when the region was renamed simply Mosel.

steps.prompt: How do the Saar and Ruwer differ from the Middle Mosel?
steps.explanation: Cooler conditions give steely, precise Riesling.

steps.title: Climate change
steps.body: Warmer summers since the 1990s have helped the Saar and Ruwer ripen grapes more reliably. What was once a marginal climate now gives balanced wines more often. This has made these cool tributaries even more prized for freshness.

steps.prompt: The region was renamed from Mosel-Saar-Ruwer to Mosel in 2007.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Saar is cool and windy, home of Scharzhofberg
The Ruwer is small, delicate and floral
Warmer summers have helped them ripen more reliably
